state.tuning_note: Third pull of the session in fourth gear. Heard audible pinging from mid-range through redline and the ECU pulled timing on cylinders two and three. Lifted early and did not repeat the pull.
reading_flags: knock sensor counts above the session baseline from mid-range to redline
ignition timing below the commanded table over the same span
lambda within target across the pull
coolant and intake-air temperatures within target

rationale: Both the note and the flags describe pinging, knock-sensor activity, and timing pulled in response, which is the knock category.

state.tuning_note: Third pull of the afternoon. Knock sensor stayed quiet for the whole run and no timing was pulled, so ignition is not what I am chasing. Near the top of third gear the car stumbled and the log shows a cut; pulled the plugs afterward and they were black and wet with fuel.
reading_flags: knock retard: none recorded, within target
lambda: below target from mid-range through redline
misfire count: above zero on cylinder three during the cut

rationale: Knock is mentioned only to be negated, so it does not apply. The note and flags describe both a misfire (stumble, cut, misfire count) and a rich condition (lambda below target, fuel-fouled plugs), and the stated precedence puts misfire ahead of rich.

Any change to the fuel system, roll structure, or seat mounting after the annual inspection requires a new technical inspection before the vehicle may enter the grid. An engine change that increases displacement by more than ten percent requires reclassification and a new inspection.

The contract says a step that includes both a permanent alteration and reversible actions is permanent.
